knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
set.seed(42)

```{r setup}
library(rwidetable)
```

## What is a WIDETABLE?

A `data.frame` lives entirely in memory, so a table with tens of thousands of
columns (for example one feature per variable and time window) quickly becomes too
big to handle. A `WIDETABLE` keeps such a table **on disk, one file per column**:

```
<path>/<name>/
    .meta.rds        # column names, classes, sizes and the number of rows
    age.rds          # one file per column
    income.rds
    ...
```

Only the columns you use are read, and a size-limited in-memory cache keeps the
most recently used ones. The number of columns is therefore limited only by the
disk space, while the object still behaves very much like a `data.frame`:
`wt[rows, cols]`, `wt[[col]]`, `nrow()`, `ncol()`, `head()`, `rbind()`, `cbind()`,
`as.data.frame()` and the `dplyr` verbs `select()` and `pull()` all work.

`WIDETABLE` is a *reference class*: an object is a handle to the table on disk.
Every change (new columns, new rows, new values) is written to the files
immediately; there is no separate save step, and copies of the handle see the same
files.

In this vignette all tables are created in a temporary folder:

```{r}
home = file.path(tempdir(), 'widetables')
dir.create(home, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 1. Building a WIDETABLE and feeding data into it

### From a data.frame in one step

`as.WIDETABLE()` creates the table folder and writes every column:

```{r}
cars = as.WIDETABLE(mtcars, name = 'cars', path = home)
cars
```

The folder now contains one file per column plus the metadata file:

```{r}
list.files(file.path(home, 'cars'), all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)
```

### Column by column

Create an empty table with `WIDETABLE()` and add vectors with the `add_column()`
method, data.frames with `add_table()`, or simply assign new columns with `[[<-`.
The first column defines the number of rows; every later column must have the same
length.

```{r}
people = WIDETABLE(name = 'people', path = home)
people$add_column(1:8, 'id')
people$add_table(data.frame(age    = c(23, 35, 41, 52, 29, 61, 33, 47),
                            gender = factor(c('F', 'M', 'F', 'F', 'M', 'M', 'F', 'M'))))
people[['joined']] <- as.Date('2020-01-01') + c(10, 400, 35, 900, 120, 2, 760, 55)
dim(people)
head(people, 3)
```

Column names must be valid file names: characters such as `/ \ : * ? " < > |` are
rejected, and so are names that differ from an existing column only by case (they
would collide on Windows and macOS).

### A really wide table

Nothing changes when the table has thousands of columns. Here we add 2,000 feature
columns, one at a time, without ever holding them all in memory:

```{r}
features = WIDETABLE(name = 'features', path = home, size_limit = 2e6)
features$add_column(1:500, 'id')
for (k in 1:2000) {
  features$add_column(rnorm(500), sprintf('f%04d', k), save_meta = FALSE)
}
features$write_meta()     # write the metadata once at the end
dim(features)
```

`save_meta = FALSE` skips rewriting the metadata file after every column, which
makes adding thousands of columns faster; `write_meta()` saves it at the end
(`add_table()` does this automatically).

`size_limit` (in bytes, default 1 GB) bounds the memory used by the cache. It is
also the threshold that decides what subsetting returns (see section 4).

### Opening an existing table

A table is opened again by name and path. Only the small metadata file is read, so
opening is instant whatever the size of the table:

```{r}
features2 = WIDETABLE(name = 'features', path = home)
dim(features2)
ncol(features2$data)   # no column is in memory yet
```

Folders written by older versions of the package (without `.meta.rds`) are scanned
once when opened, and the metadata file is created.

### From files on disk

* `parquet2WIDETABLE()` converts a folder of parquet files (for example a table
  written by Spark) into a `WIDETABLE` without loading the whole table: columns are
  processed in batches of `buffer_size`. It requires the `arrow` package.
* `RDS2Columns()` and `RData2Columns()` do the same for a folder of row chunks saved
  as `.rds` or `.RData` files.

```{r}
chunks = file.path(home, 'chunks')
dir.create(chunks)
saveRDS(iris[1:50, ],   file.path(chunks, 'part1.rds'))
saveRDS(iris[51:100, ], file.path(chunks, 'part2.rds'))
saveRDS(iris[101:150, ], file.path(chunks, 'part3.rds'))

RDS2Columns(chunks, file.path(home, 'iris'))
flowers = WIDETABLE(name = 'iris', path = home)
dim(flowers)
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# A Spark output folder with part-*.snappy.parquet files:
wt = parquet2WIDETABLE('data/features.parquet', name = 'features', path = 'tables',
                       buffer_size = 200)
```

## 2. Converting between data.frames and WIDETABLEs

| From | To | How |
|------|----|-----|
| `data.frame`, tibble, matrix | `WIDETABLE` | `as.WIDETABLE(df, name, path)` |
| `data.frame` | existing `WIDETABLE` (new columns) | `wt$add_table(df)` or `cbind(wt, df)` |
| `data.frame` | existing `WIDETABLE` (new rows) | `rbind(wt, df)` |
| `WIDETABLE` | `data.frame` | `as.data.frame(wt)`, `wt[rows, cols]` |
| `WIDETABLE` | `matrix` | `as.matrix(wt)` |

```{r}
df = as.data.frame(people)
str(df)
all.equal(as.data.frame(cars), mtcars, check.attributes = FALSE)
```

`as.WIDETABLE()` refuses to overwrite an existing table unless you ask for it:

```{r, error = TRUE}
as.WIDETABLE(mtcars, name = 'cars', path = home)
```

```{r}
cars = as.WIDETABLE(mtcars, name = 'cars', path = home, overwrite = TRUE)
```

`as.data.frame()` and `as.matrix()` load *all* columns: use them only when the
result fits in memory. Otherwise work on a subset (section 4).

## 3. Binding data frames incrementally

Data often arrive in batches: one file per day, one query result per month, one
chunk per worker. `rbind()` appends rows to a `WIDETABLE` in place, so the full
table never has to be in memory. Columns are matched by name (their order does not
matter), and factor levels are merged.

```{r}
monthly = function(month) {
  data.frame(month  = month,
             store  = sample(c('north', 'south', 'east'), 4, replace = TRUE),
             sales  = round(runif(4, 100, 500)),
             online = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 4, replace = TRUE))
}

sales = WIDETABLE(name = 'sales', path = home)   # empty table
for (m in month.abb[1:3]) {
  rbind(sales, monthly(m))                        # appended and saved
}
dim(sales)
table(sales[['month']])
```

Several tables can be bound in one call, and another `WIDETABLE` can be bound too:

```{r}
rbind(sales, monthly('Apr'), monthly('May'))
q3 = as.WIDETABLE(rbind(monthly('Jul'), monthly('Aug')), name = 'q3', path = home)
rbind(sales, q3)
nrow(sales)
```

By default the column sets must be identical. With `fill = TRUE`, missing values
are filled with `NA` and new columns are added (with `NA` for the earlier rows):

```{r, error = TRUE}
june = transform(monthly('Jun'), returns = c(2, 0, 1, 3))
rbind(sales, june)
```

```{r}
rbind(sales, june, fill = TRUE)
tail(sales, 6)
```

The equivalent method is `sales$rbind_table(df, fill = TRUE)`.

Columns can be bound in the same way with `cbind()` (or `add_table()`); the new
columns must have one value per row:

```{r}
cbind(sales, data.frame(row_id = seq_len(nrow(sales))))
colnames(sales)
```

To add columns by key rather than by position, use a left join. Row count and
order are preserved, unmatched rows get `NA`, and the key must be unique in the
joined table:

```{r}
targets = data.frame(store = c('north', 'south', 'east'), target = c(300, 250, 400))
sales$leftjoin_dataframe(targets, by = 'store')
head(sales[c('store', 'sales', 'target')])
```

## 4. Working with a WIDETABLE like a data.frame

### Dimensions and names

```{r}
dim(cars); nrow(cars); ncol(cars)
colnames(cars)
```

### Subsetting

`[` follows the `data.frame` rules: `wt[i, j]` selects rows and columns (by
position, negative position, logical vector or, for columns, by name), `wt[j]`
selects columns, and `drop = TRUE` (the default) turns a single selected column into
a vector.

```{r}
cars[1:3, c('mpg', 'cyl', 'hp')]
cars[c('mpg', 'wt')] |> head(3)
cars[cars[['cyl']] == 6, 'mpg']
cars[-(1:28), 1:3]
cars[1:2, 'mpg', drop = FALSE]
```

`[[` extracts one column as a vector:

```{r}
summary(cars[['hp']])
```

The result of `[` is a `data.frame` when its estimated size fits in
`size_limit`. When it does not, `[` returns a **new WIDETABLE** that refers to the
selected rows and columns of the same files. Nothing is read from disk until you use
it, and it can be subset further:

```{r}
small_cache = WIDETABLE(name = 'features', path = home, size_limit = 1e5)
block = small_cache[1:100, sprintf('f%04d', 1:1000)]
class(block)
dim(block)
block[1:3, 1:4]
```

`extract.widetable()` always returns a `WIDETABLE` and `extract.dataframe()` always
returns a `data.frame`, whatever the size.

### head, tail and dplyr

```{r}
head(cars, 3)
tail(cars, 2)
```

`dplyr::select()` accepts all tidyselect helpers, and `dplyr::pull()` extracts a
column:

```{r}
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
flowers |> select(starts_with('Petal')) |> head(3)
flowers |> select(where(is.factor)) |> nrow()
flowers |> pull(Species) |> table()
```

### Changing values and columns

Assignment works as for a `data.frame`, and changes are saved right away:

```{r}
cars[1:2, 'mpg'] <- 0                          # replace values
cars[['kpl']]    <- cars[['mpg']] * 0.425      # new column
cars[cars[['hp']] > 200, 'fast'] <- TRUE       # new column, NA elsewhere
cars[1:3, c('mpg', 'kpl', 'fast')]
cars[['fast']] <- NULL                         # delete a column
cars$rename_column('kpl', 'km_per_litre')
colnames(cars)
```

Assignments to a row subset change only those rows of the files:

```{r}
first10 = extract.widetable(cars, rows = 1:10)
first10[1, 'hp'] <- 999
cars[1:2, 'hp']                                    # the parent sees the change
WIDETABLE(name = 'cars', path = home)[1:2, 'hp']   # and so does the file
```

### Statistics on many columns

Any function can be applied column by column with `wt[[col]]`, so only one column
is in memory at a time:

```{r}
means = vapply(colnames(features)[-1], function(cn) mean(features[[cn]]), numeric(1))
head(means)
```

`cor.widetable()` computes the correlation matrix of all numeric columns block by
block, keeping only two blocks in memory; `cor.widetable.multicore()` computes the
blocks in parallel:

```{r}
cm = cor.widetable(cars)
round(cm[1:4, 1:4], 2)
```

### Memory management

The cache holds the most recently used columns up to `size_limit` bytes. You can
inspect it, change the limit or empty it:

```{r}
names(features$data) |> length()
features$size_limit = 5e5
features$control_size()     # applies the new limit
features$clear()            # empties the cache
```

## 5. Reference semantics: things to keep in mind

* `wt2 = wt` does **not** copy the table: both names point to the same object and
  files. To keep a separate version, copy the folder (or build a new table).
* Modifying methods (`add_column()`, `rbind()`, `[<-`, ...) write to disk
  immediately.
* A subset `WIDETABLE` (from `[` or `extract.widetable()`) shares the files of its
  parent. Changing values through it changes the parent table, and the caches of
  the parent, its copies and its subsets are refreshed automatically. Adding rows or
  columns must be done on the full table.
* A handle opened separately with `WIDETABLE(name, path)` does not see later
  changes made through another handle: call `wt$refresh()` to re-read the metadata
  and empty the cache.
* To delete a table, delete its folder: `unlink(file.path(path, name), recursive = TRUE)`.

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Method reference

| Method | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `WIDETABLE(name, path, size_limit, format)` | create or open a table |
| `as.WIDETABLE(df, name, path)` | convert a data.frame |
| `$add_column(vec, name)`, `$add_table(df)`, `cbind()` | add columns |
| `rbind(wt, df, fill)`, `$rbind_table(df, fill)` | add rows |
| `$leftjoin_dataframe(df, by)` | add columns by key |
| `wt[i, j]`, `wt[j]`, `wt[[j]]`, `head()`, `tail()` | read |
| `wt[i, j] <- v`, `wt[[j]] <- v` | write |
| `$remove_column(cn)`, `wt[[j]] <- NULL`, `$rename_column(old, new)` | manage columns |
| `$load_column(cn)`, `$load_columns(cols)` | load columns |
| `$clear()`, `$control_size()`, `$refresh()` | cache and metadata |
| `cor.widetable()`, `cor.widetable.multicore()` | correlation matrix |
